summary: A humorous, satirical piece dated October 17, 2023 that pokes fun at folk magic and common superstitions, from moon-brewed love potions to black cats, broken mirrors, salt tossing, frog warts and knocking on wood. Each section features a quirky named character and a dated, tongue-in-cheek anecdote. It closes by asking whether folklore offers comforting rituals or is a relic of imagination trumping empirical evidence.
one_line: A satirical October 2023 tour of folk superstitions, such as love potions, black cats, broken mirrors and salt tossing, using comic fictional characters.
key_facts: The article is dated October 17, 2023 and treats folk magic and superstitions as regional folklore, with a humorous tone.
Cecilia Faye, nicknamed "Moonbeam Cece" and a self-proclaimed "Moon Whisperer" from Whispers Hollow, held a seminar on September 21, 2023 about the moon's influence on love potions.
Cecilia Faye claims that collecting morning dew at midnight under a waxing gibbous moon can summon a whirlwind romance.
Bob "Lucky" McGee of Seven Hedges Lane had a black cat cross his path just after midnight on Friday the 13th, stepped forward anyway, and nothing happened.

Sandra "Biters" Jennings, keynote speaker at a September 18, 2023 convention at the Community Center of Old Tales, proposed swapping teeth for cryptocurrency, and digital wallet sales reportedly soared among under-10s.
Tim "Tough Luck" Tumbler toppled a mirror on September 29, 2023 and then planned his every move for seven years to avoid the supposed bad luck.
Geraldine "Spice" Sprinkler became a serial "salt tosser" who caused panic in restaurants, with over-the-shoulder assault cases reported by local police on October 2nd, 2023.

The Myth Busting Society (MBS), fronted by Richard "Ribbit" Hopkins, met on November 1st, 2023 to debunk the frog-and-wart myth, with Hopkins saying "We've touched all the frogs, kissed a few, and still, no warts."
TV personality Johnny "Knock-Knock" Woodbine declared on September 14th, 2023 that obsessive knocking on wood explained his success, yet his show was canceled the following week due to low ratings.
The article ends by asking whether superstitions are comforting rituals in an unpredictable world or remnants of a time when imagination trumped empirical evidence.
